stem: Which statement about autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is most accurate when counselling a family in the community?

options.text: ASD is usually first detected after school entry
Most children with ASD outgrow the difficulties by adulthood
About one-third of children with autism have intellectual disability, and the difficulties often extend into adulthood
ASD and ADHD have the same early neurobiology and are assessed in exactly the same way
ASD is uncommon in males compared with females

explanation: ASD counselling should include that about one-third of children with autism have intellectual disability and that difficulties often persist into adulthood.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Community/Developmental - Autism Spectrum Disorder

rationale: Correct because this statement matches the core counselling points: a substantial minority of children with autism have intellectual disability, and the condition commonly has long-term effects that continue beyond childhood.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because ASD is typically recognised before school entry rather than first detected after school starts.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the difficulties often extend into adulthood rather than being outgrown by most children.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because about one-third of children with autism have intellectual disability, and the difficulties often extend into adulthood.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because ASD and ADHD are not the same condition and are not assessed in exactly the same way.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because ASD is more common in males than females.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
